notes: Read the service target, full preceding civic context, all fourteen candidates and the review. Restored the Democratic Party as the proposing actor rather than inventing an administration. Restored the omitted account of military service and the call to make service possible for all citizens. Anchored the invest-in-America exchange to service and named its support mechanisms, and resolved the concluding methods to the listed service measures.

claims.claim_text: The Democratic Party would ask all Americans to participate actively in meeting the new century's challenges.
The U.S. military had answered calls to serve in the young century even though those calls came too often.
The United States must make service possible for all citizens.
The Democratic Party would expand AmeriCorps.
The Democratic Party would double the Peace Corps.
The Democratic Party would enable more Americans to serve in the military.
The Democratic Party would create new international-service opportunities.
The Democratic Party would integrate service into primary education.
The Democratic Party would create new service opportunities for experienced and retired people.

In exchange for Americans' service, the Democratic Party would increase service-learning support, offer tax incentives to college students who serve, and create scholarships for students pledging to become teachers.
The Democratic Party would use the Internet to match volunteers more effectively with service opportunities.
The listed service measures would unleash service's power to address U.S. challenges in a distinctly American way.
